verdict.rationale: Kong's AI Gateway positions itself as an 'MCP Traffic Gateway' that can govern, secure, and observe traffic to/from MCP servers, and its Catalog can inventory MCP servers alongside APIs and agents (kong-docs-65, kong-docs-22, kong-gh-6). However, the evidence centers on Kong auto-generating/exposing MCP servers from REST APIs and proxying/governing MCP traffic between agents and servers, not on Kong itself acting as an MCP client that plugs in external MCP servers to consume their tools directly. Missing for 10: clear documentation of Kong itself invoking/using tools from a connected MCP server (client-side tool use), independent/hands-on confirmation of this workflow, and detail on how a user 'plugs in' an arbitrary third-party MCP server for Kong's own use.
